chunks: And I have come to know that a man from them
would enter upon a Muslim woman, and another under treaty (protection)
and would take away her leg ornaments, armlets, necklaces, and ear-rings
from which she could not resist except by reciting the verse of return and seeking mercy
not a single man among them was struck (wounded) nor was his blood shed
So if a Muslim man died after this of grief, he would not be blamed, but rather he would be deserving (of it) in my view.
ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about a Muslim man dying of grief after witnessing the taking of women's jewelry?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) describes a period of laxity where men from the community would enter upon Muslim and protected women, forcibly taking their jewelry (leg ornaments, armlets, necklaces, ear-rings). The women could only resist by reciting the verse of return (Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un) and pleading for mercy. They returned with their wealth, suffering no casualties or wounds. Consequently, if a Muslim man died of grief after witnessing this, he would not be blamed but rather justified.

en.sayed-ali-raza: I have come to know that
every one of them entered upon Muslim women and other women under protection of Islam
and took away their ornaments from legs, arms, necks and ears
and no woman could resist it except by pronouncing the verse, “We are for Allāh and to Him we shall return.” (Qur’ān, 2:156)
Then they got back laden with wealth
without any wound or loss of life.
If any Muslim dies of grief after all this he is not to be blamed but rather there is justification for him before me.
